match.reason: Neither bank point covers the environmental and sustainability impacts of trade, such as cleaner technology spread and waste and emissions from cheap goods; they only explain what trade links are and how Australia's partners have changed.

draft.title: Trade and sustainability
card: Trade can spread cleaner technology. A country can buy solar panels or electric buses made elsewhere, which can help it cut its emissions.
Trade also makes goods cheap, such as fast fashion and electronics. Cheap goods are often bought in large numbers and thrown out quickly.
This adds to waste, because old clothes and devices pile up in landfill. Much of the waste can end up in other countries.
Making more goods also uses more energy, water and raw materials, and releases emissions. Much of this happens in the countries that make the goods.
draft.remember: Trade can spread clean technology, but cheap goods can add to waste, emissions and resource use abroad.

a.q: Why can trade in fast fashion harm sustainability?
opts: Cheap clothes are bought and thrown out in large amounts
Trade stops countries from sharing any new technology
Clothes made overseas use no energy or water to produce
Fewer clothes are made when they are sold across borders
a.why: Cheap clothes encourage people to buy many items and discard them quickly. That adds to waste, and making them uses resources. Trade can still share technology, so the second option is wrong.
a.clue: Think about what happens to cheap clothes after a few wears.

b.q: Which example shows trade helping sustainability?
opts: A country buys imported solar panels to cut its emissions
A shop sells more cheap phones that people replace yearly
A factory uses more water to make extra imported shirts
Old electronics are shipped overseas and left in landfill
b.why: Imported solar panels are cleaner technology spread through trade, and they can help cut emissions. The other options each add to waste or resource use.
b.clue: Look for the option that spreads cleaner technology.

a.best: Cheap clothes are bought and thrown out in large amounts

b.best: A country buys imported solar panels to cut its emissions

problems.detail: Why (a) says the 'second option' is wrong because trade can share technology. The options are in random order, and here the second option is about clothes using no energy or water. The technology option is the third. The why should name the option by its content, not its position.
